clue.text: Ignore first of letters penned by lender

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
something penned is shut in a pen, so one piece sits enclosed inside another

blocks.note: a bank is an institution that lends money
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone advises disregarding the first of the letters a moneylender has written.
explanation.walkthrough: The L goes inside BANK, after its B. 'Ignore' is a verb here, as in to blank someone you pass in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To blank a person is informal usage for deliberately snubbing or pretending not to see them.

clue.text: US city extra supportive of a spin-off of Indian cuisine

blocks.note: balti is a curry style developed in Birmingham, an offshoot of Indian cooking
extra means additional

explanation.surface: A city that backs a new Indian food trend with extra enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece 'supportive of' another sits below it. A balti is a curry served in a small wok-like pan, popularised in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a major port city in the state of Maryland, on Chesapeake Bay.

clue.text: Deleted content of appalling Grok – endless trouble

indicators.note: with the contents deleted, only the shell of the word survives: its two outer letters
having no end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
the name of the AI chatbot, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Offensive output from the Grok chatbot gets deleted, causing no end of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: AG plus GRO makes AGGRO. Grok is Elon Musk's AI chatbot, whose posts have sometimes been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation, meaning hostile trouble, fighting or hassle.

clue.text: Russian spymaster forgets line, fine start to evening singsong!

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so a letter drops away
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: Karla is the Soviet spymaster in John le Carré's Smiley novels
L is the abbreviation for line
OK means fine
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A spy chief fluffs his line, but the evening's sing-along starts well.
explanation.walkthrough: Karla is the Soviet spy chief in John le Carré's Smiley novels. The exclamation mark covers a cheery sing-along night.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is a social entertainment where amateurs sing along to recorded backing tracks, a modern communal sing-along.

clue.text: Full of energy – vroom! – led Wacky Races here

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to a place, standing for a noun

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside
wacky means crazy and erratic, so the letters are put into a madcap new order

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An energetic cartoon car revs up and leads the field in the TV show Wacky Races.
explanation.walkthrough: Wacky Races is an old Hanna-Barbera cartoon; here 'Wacky' is the signal and 'Races here' defines. 'Races' does double duty in the surface and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is an arena with a banked oval track built for cycle racing, so contests happen there.

clue.text: Taking name of aggressive woman

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: aggressive means given to violence
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A violent woman's name is being taken down, perhaps by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' looks like 'acquiring' but here it means taking away: VIOLENT without its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a female first name, and crosswords often use 'woman' or 'girl' to clue such names.

clue.text: Room height, length raised

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a letter moves it higher, swapping its place with the one above

blocks.note: altitude is height above sea level
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Describing a room: its height, and its length increased.
explanation.walkthrough: ALTITUDE has its L moved up one place, above the A, to give LATITUDE. The clue reads like dimensions of a room, but 'Room' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or freedom of action, which is room to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Detectives arresting emperor? Flipping severe!

indicators.note: arresting someone takes them into custody, so one piece is held inside the other
to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of UK police
a tsar was a Russian emperor

explanation.surface: Police detectives arrest an emperor, and an onlooker exclaims at how harsh it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor goes inside the detectives before the whole is turned round. 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, as in 'flipping heck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme and harsh, which is a close synonym of severe.

clue.text: Dungeon in Paris where Ms Davis necks large one

indicators.note: to neck something is to swallow it down, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: French for 'where'
Bette Davis, the Hollywood film star
L is the abbreviation for large
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In a Paris cellar, the actress Bette Davis knocks back a large drink.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck a drink is British slang for swallowing it quickly; here BETTE swallows L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in its ceiling, a name from French oublier, to forget.

clue.text: Go into two hospital departments

blocks.note: tells the solver to join two pieces; it supplies no letters itself
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department, the first of the two
ER is the emergency room, the second of the two hospital departments

explanation.surface: A patient is told to go into two different hospital departments.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT treats ears, noses and throats; ER is the American emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is simply to go into it, a plain synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Beery yobbo Elgar sozzled, left unconscious

indicators.note: sozzled means very drunk, and a drunk's letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: the English composer's name
L is the abbreviation for left
out cold means unconscious

explanation.surface: A drunk lout sees the composer Elgar so plastered he passes out.
explanation.walkthrough: A yobbo is a British word for a rowdy young hooligan, so the whole first phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager lout is a British term for a young man who turns rowdy and violent after drinking beer.

clue.text: Circuit breaker initially installed in atomic science college

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
something installed is fitted inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: A as in A-bomb, the atomic bomb
opening letter of the word
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A circuit breaker is fitted in the labs of a college of nuclear science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuit breaker' looks like one electrical item, but 'Circuit' alone is the definition, in its sense of a boundary or sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or bounds of something, like a circuit marking the edge of an area.

clue.text: Press yellow base metal made from this?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer, standing for a noun

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
or is gold, the heraldic yellow
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A question about pressing a yellowish base metal out of some raw material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base metal' looks like one phrase, but 'base' is wordplay and 'metal made from this?' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is the rock mined and smelted to extract the metal iron, its raw source.

clue.text: Cheaper looking Scottish spud set before king

blocks.note: tattie is the Scots word for potato
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A humble Scottish potato served up before a king looks rather downmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Spud is an informal word for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby or worn, so something tattier appears more down-at-heel and inferior.

clue.text: Opening discount store

blocks.note: first meaning: a vent or exit through which something escapes
second meaning: a shop selling goods cheaply, often direct from the maker

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the launch of a bargain shop; 'Opening' is a noun meaning a way out, not an event.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a physical vent for release and a retail shop selling surplus or reduced goods.

clue.text: Extremely liberal mother, one rejected by Starmer and Starmer’s father?

indicators.note: what is rejected is thrown out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: too means excessively
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
ma is an informal word for mother
Keir Starmer, the British Prime Minister, by first name
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wry question about Keir Starmer's family: a very liberal mother and an unnamed father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely liberal' looks like one description but splits in two. Starmer is used twice, once for his first name and once in the definition, which the setter clearly intends.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer has often mentioned that his father worked as a toolmaker in a factory.

clue.text: As he left the Sorbonne, le duc ate dainty sandwiches

definitions.note: a clause describing his state, standing for an adjective

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between slices, so the letters lie inside the words around them

blocks.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A French duke, graduating from the Sorbonne, eats delicate sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food the duke ate, but it is a verb. The Sorbonne is a famous Paris university.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaving a university has been through schooling, so they are learned and schooled.

clue.text: Unsafe, rickety garden house with peeling walls

indicators.note: rickety means falling to pieces, so the letters are rebuilt in a new arrangement
with its walls peeled off, a word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the word minus its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shaky summerhouse with flaking walls is a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden house' looks like one building, but 'garden' is the shuffled part and 'house' loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous means likely to cause harm, the plain opposite of safe.

clue.text: Lops head off flowering plant

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener deadheads a plant by cutting off its flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lops head off' looks like an instruction to delete a first letter, but 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily family plant with spikes of white or yellow blooms, the flower of the Greek underworld.

clue.text: Character in shocking film dealing with erotic s*x

indicators.note: dealing cards follows a shuffle, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
the starred-out word keeps only its two printed letters

explanation.surface: A notorious horror film handles erotic sex, with the word coyly censored.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisk is a censor's mark, so only S and X count. The Exorcist is the 1973 horror film, and Father Merrin is its title character.
explanation.definitionFit: The exorcist, a priest who drives out demons, is the title role of the famously shocking horror movie.

clue.text: Truncated holiday time? On top of this, caught ailment

indicators.note: truncating cuts something short, so the end of the word is chopped off

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the full word with its last four letters deleted
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A holiday cut short, and on top of that someone caught a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, whatever sits 'on top of' the rest is written first. 'caught' reads as catching an illness, but it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an infectious bacterial disease of the intestines, spread through dirty water.

clue.text: Clergyman put back in prison in the US – a deep, dark hole

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the letters run backwards
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend
the can is American slang for jail

explanation.surface: A vicar is sent back to an American jail, which is a deep, dark hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep, dark hole' sounds like a description of a prison cell, but it defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavern is a large underground cave, a deep and gloomy hollow in rock.

clue.text: “America, China United” – Russia’s premier layman

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the leading letter is used

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America
china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend
U is the abbreviation for United, as in team names
opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A slogan of US-Chinese unity, as declared by the Russian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country, but in rhyming slang it means a friend. 'premier' looks like a head of government but means first.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a non-professional, someone without specialist training, which is what a layman is.

clue.text: Period at school not as busy?

blocks.note: less means to a smaller degree than
when a lot is on, things are busy

explanation.surface: A question: is a school period quieter than the rest of the day?
explanation.walkthrough: Something with less on is not as busy; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a timetabled class in school, one of the periods of the teaching day.

clue.text: Huge US subject visited by male doctor

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: math is the American short form of mathematics
M is the abbreviation for male
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A huge American school subject is inspected by a male doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say math where the British say maths; MO, a medical officer, is a common crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means enormous, from the giant prehistoric elephant.

clue.text: Signified average temperature

blocks.note: the mean is the arithmetic average
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A forecaster's average temperature was a sign of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'average temperature' looks like a weather phrase, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: What a word signified is what it meant; both are past tenses of verbs for expressing sense.

clue.text: Former partner, full-figured specimen

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
ample describes a generous, curvy build

explanation.surface: Someone describes their ex as a fine, curvaceous specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specimen' reads as a remark about a person but defines the answer as a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single sample taken as typical of its kind, which is an example.

clue.text: Pascal Lamy regularly censored sacred hymn

indicators.note: censoring at regular intervals blots out every other letter, leaving alternate ones

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: The former trade chief Pascal Lamy keeps having a sacred hymn censored.
explanation.walkthrough: Pascal Lamy is a French politician who led the World Trade Organization.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Joint continued to irritate when uncovered

indicators.note: uncovering strips away the outside, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: to rankle is to keep causing resentment

explanation.surface: A sore joint kept irritating its owner once it was bared.
explanation.walkthrough: RANKLED loses its R and D to leave ANKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge joint connecting the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Adores Depp, mostly playing an outlaw

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
playing a part means taking on a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the actor's surname without its last letter

explanation.surface: A fan adores Johnny Depp, mostly when he plays an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like Depp acting a role, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit of the Wild West, a criminal on the run.

clue.text: Seaman quietly ‘eavin’ heavy-duty cover

blocks.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
heaving means hauling; dropping the opening H and final G in Cockney style gives the clipped form

explanation.surface: A sailor, speaking in dialect, quietly heaves a big waterproof sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes in the clue show dropped letters, so the synonym must drop them too: hauling becomes 'aulin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large sheet of waterproof canvas or plastic used to protect things from weather.

clue.text: Legendary Roman figure displayed in Louvre museum

indicators.note: an exhibit displayed in a gallery sits within it, so the letters lie inside the run of words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A statue of a legendary Roman is on show at the Louvre in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Louvre does hold Roman sculpture, so the surface is plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Remus was the twin brother of Romulus in the myth of Rome's founding, raised by a she-wolf.
